checks.title: A deployer revokes a mailbox and every session logged in to it is told and closed, while other mailboxes are untouched
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: A deployer revokes a mailbox and every session on it ends
  Given mailbox "team@example.test" has two users with different valid passwords
  And a mail client is logged in to it over IMAP as the first user and has not selected a folder
  And a mail client is logged in to it over IMAP as the second user and has selected INBOX
  And a mail client is logged in to it over IMAP and has gone idle long enough to hibernate
  And a mail client is logged in to it for submission
  And a mail client is logged in over IMAP to another mailbox "other@example.test"
  When the deployer revokes mailbox "team@example.test"
  Then each of the four clients on "team@example.test" receives a BYE and its connection closes
  And none of them can read or send mail on the closed connection
  And the client on "other@example.test" stays connected and can still fetch its mail
  And each user of "team@example.test" can log in again with their valid password and read mail
proves: FR-MAIL-049 SHALL 1: every IMAP and submission session logged in to it, awake or hibernating, is told and closed
FR-MAIL-049 SHALL 1: a session registers with its mailbox at login and not at SELECT (the unselected session)
FR-MAIL-049 SHALL 2: revocation is per mailbox, so another valid password's session also closes and reconnects
toy 01a1a4c4 refuted claim: a logged-in unselected session stayed open and read mail after revoke, 5 of 5 (seen failure, kept)
toy 01a1a4c4 must_hold: register a session at login, not at SELECT
toy 01a1ae1d: the hibernating session is made by evict with webSockets 'hibernate' after the last reply is read, never by ctx.abort(), which drops the socket and is not hibernation
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A deployer and the mail clients meet this through public surfaces over several calls (log in, select, revoke, observe close, reconnect), so it is one whole behaviour, not one rule.

checks.title: A session whose registration with its mailbox fails is not logged in
checks.rule: LOGIN answers OK only after the session's registration with its mailbox has succeeded; when registration throws or never completes, the session stays unauthenticated and the client gets no OK.
checks.unit: ImapSession login handling (and the submission session's equivalent), calling ImapMailbox.register
proves: FR-MAIL-049 SHALL 1: every session logged in to it is told and closed; a logged-in session that never registered cannot be found by revoke, so this outcome is settled (the spec-writer's worked example)
Decision 01a1a48e: revocation wraps every strategy, so registration sits after any strategy's login answer
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The failure needs an injected fault in the mailbox's session registry, which no public surface can cause, and the rule shows in a single LOGIN call.

checks.title: One session that fails to close does not stop revoke closing the rest
checks.rule: When telling or closing one registered session throws, ImapMailbox.revoke still tells and closes every other registered session, and counts the one that failed under failed.
proves: FR-MAIL-049 SHALL 1: every session logged in to it is told and closed
toy 01a1a4c4 signature: revoke(): Promise<{ told; closed; failed }>
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A session object that throws on close, or a stale registration left by a session that already ended, can only be staged inside the mailbox, and the happy-path scenario never enters that path.

gaps.failure_way: Telling or closing one session fails and that session stays open
gaps.question: When revoke cannot tell or close a session, what must happen: retry until it is closed, close it without a BYE, or report it as failed to the deployer and stop? Each answer leaves SHALL 1 true or false differently, and the choice changes what revoke returns to the deployer.

gaps.failure_way: The mailbox cannot read its registered sessions when revoke runs
gaps.question: When revoke cannot read the mailbox's registered sessions, does the deployer get an error and try again, or does mail retry on its own? SHALL 3 promises no close time, so both keep the SHALLs true, but the deployer surface differs.

gaps.failure_way: A login is in flight while the deployer revokes
gaps.question: Does a login that started before revoke and completes after it count as logged in at revocation, and so must be closed, or is it a new session that may stay, since revoke does not lock the mailbox (SHALL 2: sessions reconnect)? The answer decides whether register and revoke must be ordered against each other.
